# Evidence index

**Generated by `tools/neoforge-evidence`. Do not hand-edit.**
Fix the tag where it is written and re-run, or this file and the claims
it indexes drift apart - which is the failure it exists to prevent.

NeoForge tags every claim with its standard of evidence. The convention
is applied carefully in each file and, until this index existed, nowhere
centrally - so a soft claim was visible only to whoever happened to read
the file carrying it. Weakest first, because those have work attached.

### `docs/why-the-split.md`

- **L10**  
  Everything below marked is inference from the hardware, not
- **L71**  
  A smaller edge connector is cheaper, physically smaller, and has fewer contacts to oxidise or misalign. In a consumer product sold into living rooms and handled by children, all three matter considerably more than they do on an arcade PCB inside a locked cabinet.
- **L83**  
  For an arcade format where cartridges vastly outnumber motherboards, on the board is not a close call.
- **L146**  
  That said, the friction was real regardless of intent**, and it is hard to imagine SNK minding. It is exactly why MVS-to-AES converters cannot be passive devices. A convenient side effect is not the same as a design goal — but it is not evidence against one either. We simply have no source.
- **L229**  
  Worth looking for in the next NeoSD photograph.** The [`prior-art.md`](prior-art.md) entry notes pin headers along the left edge of `NEOSD_PRO_AES_PROG`. Those are probably programming and debug access - but if any of them is a board-to-board link, that answers which of the three a shipping product chose, and it is a cheap thing to look for.

  Signal → board face | — A, B and C agree |
- **L245**  
  Signal names | — all three agree |
- **L246**

- **L247**

- **L260**  
  The audio-loop duplication was real, not a misreading.** A shows `L in`/`L out` on both top faces and `R out`/`R in` on both bottom faces. C shows all four pairs **unconnected** on the AES 3.5 — corroborating the wiki's note that these loops are "only used on the NEO-AES board revision." Two sources, agreeing, on a detail that looked like a transcription error.

### `docs/cartridge-architecture.md`

- **L23** — *wiki NEO-ZMC2, LSPC2-A2*  
  Sprite pixel data must be serialized before reaching the video chain. The serializer takes the C ROM data bus as C0~C31 (two 16-bit halves), which supplies all pixel data for an 8-pixel line, clocked by EVEN1, EVEN2, H and LOAD from the LSPC, returning DOTA/DOTB pixel opacity to it.
- **L28** — *wiki MVS cartridge*  
  complete C ROM data bus at the edge connector, and the board's chip serializes it. Because NEO-ZMC2 is not present in the cart, plain NEO-ZMC handles M1 ROM bankswitching instead.
- **L33** — *wiki AES cartridge*  
  NEO-ZMC2 or PRO-CT0. The wiki states plainly that this is the reason MVS-to-AES converters cannot be passive devices.
- **L56** — *wiki PRO-CT0*  
  PRO-CT0 | Early gate array. Also sold as **SNK-9201** and **ALPHA-8921** (original Alpha Denshi name, from their Alpha68k system). Serializes sprite graphics in AES carts and MVS boards. |
- **L57** — *wiki NEO-ZMC2*  
  NEO-ZMC2 | NEO-ZMC (Z80 bankswitching) + PRO-CT0 (serializer) in one package. Found in second-revision MVS boards for the PRO-CT0 logic only, and in AES cartridges. |
- **L58** — *MAME neogeo.c chip notes, sourced from wiki*  
  NEO-CMC | Later replacement. The 90G06CF7042 variant bundles NEO-273 logic, NEO-ZMC logic, C-ROM decryption, C and S-ROM multiplexing, and S-ROM bankswitching. The CF7050 variant adds M-ROM decryption. |
- **L63** — *wiki NEO-B1*  
  Downstream, NEO-B1 receives serialized sprite graphics from the multiplexer (NEO-ZMC2, PRO-CT0 or NEO-CMC) while fix-layer graphics come directly from the enabled fix ROM. Two pixels are written at a time into internal line buffers.

- **L133** — *wiki PROGBK1*  
  A 27C322 cannot be used as a V ROM.** The V ROM data bus is 8-bit — byte mode — and the 27C322 only operates in word mode. Original mask ROMs could output in byte mode; programmable 42-pin EPROMs physically lack a `/BYTE` pin. Replacing a 32 Mbit V ROM needs a different memory IC on an adapter board.

- **L101** — *ngdevkit nullsound/Makefile.in*  
  The driver links `nullsound-aes.lib` rather than the default. For this ROM that is a formality: the two variants differ only in `fm-tables.inc` and `ssg-tables.inc`, only `entrypoint.s` is assembled per-variant, and **ADPCM-A does not use those tables** — its playback rate is fixed by the YM2610's own clock.
